topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture’s subject and learning objectives before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer development through the origins and evolutionary effects of cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Evidence and interpretation of environmental cancer risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence about cancer risk supports and shapes interpretations of environmental influences.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain infection-associated carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a specific example.

topics.label: Carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular processes through which carcinogenic exposures damage DNA and produce mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and tissue-specific carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tissue conditions and susceptibility shape tumour development following carcinogenic exposure, ending with a summary of the mechanisms discussed.

topics.label: Human evidence for carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological evidence from human populations helps identify carcinogen exposure and assess carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity and mutagenicity testing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine laboratory tests used to assess carcinogenic potential and the limitations of their results.

topics.label: Lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing its main conclusions about cancer risks and their assessment.
